items.frozen_body: Recovering Lorentz signature requires an imaginary-time-direction degree of freedom assigned a Higgs role.
In that formulation, Euclidean left-handed spinors acquire an internal SU(2) role.
W04a proposes using only the right-handed spinor kind for spacetime vectors in both Minkowski and Euclidean signatures.
Euclidean spacetime is associated with extra fibration/real-structure data rather than the same real form as Minkowski spacetime.
In W04c, Wick rotation becomes a gauge-like extra choice, and the left chiral symmetry is interpreted internally before that choice.
W04d identifies complex-time holomorphy / boundary values as the essence of Wick rotation and says there is no distinguished Euclidean target without extra structure.

W01 explicitly distinguishes this construction from conventional GUT unification: it does not place all gauge groups into one larger Lie group and does not identify a generation with a single usual GUT spinor representation.
W04c interprets Wick rotation as an extra choice of CP1 fibration/imaginary-time direction rather than a fundamental Euclidean-to-Minkowski coordinate substitution.

In the right-handed Euclidean description SU(2)_L behaves as an internal rather than spacetime symmetry; W02 treats this as a possible route toward interaction unification, while distinguishing it from earlier Minkowski gravi-weak proposals.
